item.title: Audit of heavy claims — what needs to be removed from the text?
item.lead: The deeper monographs contain powerful figures and causal formulations. The scientific quality of the series increases if these claims are visibly reduced to their evidence status.

blocks.text: The statements regarding “78% of 200 viral videos”, “r=0.68 at n=312”, “€2,100 per month”, “r=-0.71 at n=12”, “oxytocin +150%”, “D2 -22%” and similar exact effects are not provided with a verifiable dataset, preregistration, or peer-reviewed analysis in the available source material. Therefore, they are not repeated as research results.

The formulation that a market consciously creates paranoia and then sells the solution is also an intention claim. An economic system can benefit from demand for a product without thereby proving a coordinated intention. The distinction between incentive and intention is explicitly made in this edition.

The same correction applies to the claim that adult-tech is the cause of declining fertility. OECD and UNFPA describe multiple factors — including housing, work, uncertainty, healthcare costs, partner availability, and changing preferences. Adult-tech can be investigated as a hypothesis, but the existing data do not support a singular causal conclusion.

blocks.label: EDITORIAL CORRECTION
blocks.text: Exact figures without a reproducible method are marked as unconfirmed in this edition and are not used as evidence.
Adult-tech causes low Hypothesis Longitudinal, multivariate research fertility
Coordinated paranoia strategy Hypothesis Internal strategy documents + causal design
Ghost-chatting / AI-chatting exists Documented Multiple independent sources + product documentation
